translation:
Jivanji Maharaj's most intimate and grace-favoured devotee (nij jan), the Vaishnav Krishnadasji, having received kanthi-diksha from Jivanji Maharaj, now renounces his original identity — his Brahmin lineage and his former worship of Ganpati and so on — and, taking on exclusive Vaishnav-hood, returns to Agalod by the Guru's command. This highly learned Brahmin, Krishnadasji, who had been a strict ritualist and worshipper of Omkar, has become dyed in the colour of Jivanji Maharaj and has become an exclusive Vaishnav. He wishes to remain continuously in his Guru's presence, but when the Guru's command comes for him to return home, he takes his leave and comes back to Agalod. According to the custom that was traditionally followed, Dhanaji invites Krishnadasji to a Brahmin feast (brahma bhojan), but he respectfully declines, and says:

_Ab mein ananya vrat liyo, kaahuko bartan na jaay chhuyo. To saakut ann liyo na jaai, kaise bhog lagaavu bhai._ (Now I have taken the vow of exclusive devotion — I do not even touch another's vessel. Then how could I accept the grain of a Sakut, a worshipper of Shakti? How, brother, could I offer such a thing to my gracious Lord?)

Krishnadasji says that he has now taken up the vow of exclusive devotion; he does not even touch another person's vessel, so how then could he accept the grain and so on of a Sakut (a worshipper of Shakti)? And how could he offer it to his gracious Lord (Kripanath)? This can no longer be done. Hearing these words, Dhana Patel became extremely grieved and asked the reason. Krishnadasji said, I have accepted Jivandasji as my Sadguru, and so I have now become an uda-bhakt, and I can no longer keep the company of a Sakut. Hearing this, Dhana, deeply grieved, asked to be freed himself from this cycle of the ocean of worldly existence (bhavsagar) and to be granted exclusive Vaishnav-hood. Krishnadasji said that only the Sadguru can do this. So Dhanaji, taking his son and grandson with him, under Krishnadasji's guidance, came along with him to Puniyad, and received the rosary (mala) and mark (tilak) from Jivandasji.

_Mala Jeevandaaski, mili hai diksha sang. Ghana darash dekhata, bahot chadhaayo rang._ (He received the rosary of Jivandas along with the initiation. Seeing this darshan, Dhana was overwhelmed — greatly coloured with devotion.)

In this way, when Dhana Bhagat was given the rosary and kanthi, an extraordinary colour of devotion rose in him, and thus he became an "uda-bhagat." By the command of Jivandasji, Krishnadas began showing the true path to seekers in Agalod and the surrounding villages, and giving them kanthi-diksha. For, [the Guru reasoned,] many others like Dhana Bhagat would come along later, and how many times could they keep coming to and from Puniyad? So, seeing the mettle and learning in Krishnadasji, Jivanji Maharaj told him that from now on he too should give kanthi-diksha on behalf of Namdev and Kabirji, and he said to Dhana Bhagat:

_Tab sadguru bole man laai, suno Dhana Mangala Shitlaai. Tamo mahant Krishnadaskun maano, sab santanko ye darshan cheeno._ (Then the Sadguru spoke wholeheartedly: Listen, Dhana, Mangala, and Shitala! Accept Krishnadasji as your Mahant [spiritual head]; recognize this as the teaching for all the saints.)

O Dhana, Mangala, and Shitala! From today, regard Krishnadasji as the certified head (sanchalak) of the seat (padtharo) of Namdev-Kabirji for our region. I also grant him the authority of a Guru. Consider his word equal to my own word, and conduct yourselves accordingly. Having given this command, he sent them off.

Krishnadasji went there and turned many seekers and thirsty souls into exclusive Vaishnavs, and spread the Uda faith there. Today this region is known as the Kantha area.
